registry_disposition.reason: S5 Path-Confinement follow-up run (owner ticket of 2026-10-21, four-item checklist over the MERGED result of the S5 path-confinement slice). The slice itself is not reopened: its contract, corpus, record format and digests are untouched, the S5 evaluation functionality is unchanged, and the HO-01 lane keeps its qualification without a silent expansion of its scope. Four items are covered. (1) C5: the hardlink guard read the link count only on the PATH, during the containment check, so a hardlink created in the window between that check and the open was not seen - the real path of a hardlink IS its own path, so no path-based check can observe a second name for the same inode, and the device and inode identity does not change when a second name appears, so the replacement guard cannot observe it either. The link count is now read a second time ON THE OPENED DESCRIPTOR and compared with the observed count; any difference is refused with PATH_MULTIPLE_LINKS, and a count that cannot be compared at all is refused as well. The parent-directory re-check now runs BEFORE the link-count check, because a replaced parent that carries the same file over as a hardlink would otherwise be reported as a link-count defect and would hide the parent check behind it; both branches stay independently provable. One new test binds the race. The module header's residual R1 is extended accordingly: a link created AFTER the descriptor was opened reaches the content exactly as an in-place rewrite does and is not detected. The first wording of this run said that C5 closes the window between the check and the open; the independent review REFUTED that wording and the reviewer was right - a hardlink created AND removed inside that window leaves the link count unchanged, so the descriptor check sees nlink 1 and passes, and the read returns the rewritten content. The corrected statement, now in the module header and bound by a new test, is: C5 detects a second name that still EXISTS when the descriptor is inspected; it detects neither a link created and removed inside the window nor a link created after the open, and both are R1's in-place-rewrite class, which no path or identity check could have caught either. The residual list is otherwise unchanged (R1 to R4) and none of the four is claimed as eliminated. (2) An independent delta review was run over the state that actually ships - the rebased branch, the two merge commits, the cross-lane adaptation of the S8 evidence-provenance module, and the Registry and Atlas records written against the pre-rebase commits - with three lenses, each in its own fresh context on a model different from the one that wrote the code, and one independent confirmer per finding reproducing every finding from its evidence alone. (3) The hosted CI could not be used: the account's GitHub Actions admission is still closed, and the run that belongs to the S5 merge commit itself (39550245291) carries the annotation 'The job was not started because your account is locked due to a billing issue'; the lock is account-wide, the Unitera Registry and Unitera Systems runs end in startup_failure after 0 seconds. NO HOSTED CI RESULT IS CLAIMED. The complete hosted job was instead replicated locally on the final state under the same Node version the workflow pins (v20.20.2): the syntax check of the five files, npm run validate-maws-vnext, npm run test:skill-frontdoor and node scripts/tools/ci-gate.mjs, the last answering PASS CI Gate with exit 0; npm run test:vnext answers 709/709 pass, npm run eval:skill-effectiveness answers IMPROVEMENT_PROVEN with the security gate PASS and the digests unchanged, and npm run validate-behavioral-eval answers 7 cases checked, 0 unexpected. The security scan was re-run on the final state (scan-2026-10-21T07-07-57.089Z-fc7d563aaa6f, seal sha256:3c8da16e423408db2e22727536fbafbf3a3ed3d67b581870ff6d30bb4a4e4000, 0 findings, 198 packages scanned, 2 packages matching 2 advisories) and the coverage was measured rather than merely disclosed: a copy of the repository with the four changed files removed and an otherwise identical tree produces the SAME analysed set (34 files selected, 34 parsed, 104 functions, 140 call edges, the same gap, the same 0 findings), reproduced on two independent project identifiers, and a copy without scripts/, tests/, core/, runtime/ and evals/ still yields the same 104 functions and 140 call edges and even reports complete/ completed. The whole analysed set therefore lies outside scripts/ and tests/, which is where this material lives, so the 0 findings carry NO INFORMATION ABOUT THE SLICE and NO SECURITY CLAIM is derived from the scan. A copy narrowed to the changed material analyses 0 files and reports complete/ completed; that verdict is vacuous and is deliberately not presented as better coverage. (4) The foreign Registry and Atlas drifts were attributed rather than silently repaired. Against a FRESHLY PROVISIONED mirror farm of all 17 owner repositories (scripts/ci_clone_owner_repos.py, 17/17 cloned, the CI-faithful method), the Registry reachability gate answers 617 verified current claims, 31 historical, 31 separate current observations, 8 record-gap diagnostics and 1 mismatch, and the Atlas pin gate answers 1 failure; both remaining items belong to ONE lane, the personal-pilot launch acceptance lane: the Registry record PERSONAL_PILOT_LAUNCH_ACCEPTANCE_2026_10_21_001.yaml declares source_publication.head_commit_on_default_branch false for head_commit 7db4619e although the commit IS an ancestor of baum-os origin/main, because the record was written at observed_at 2026-10-21T00:04:00Z while baum-os pull request 65 was still open and the pull request merged afterwards; and the Atlas claim C-PERSONAL-PILOT-LAUNCH-ACCEPTANCE-2026-10-21 references the path apps/api/src/governed-execution/personal-negative-gate-coverage.spec.ts, which does not exist at the claim's own pinned commit f6114ebae0bfca75843fe4d08385781190d883cf because the file was introduced later, in 76ccb430. Both are named, attributed and registered; neither is silently repaired, because the repair of a registered object of another lane belongs to the lane that owns it. The same measurement also exposed a false-drift class: against a STALE local mirror the same gates report 3 mismatches and 1 unverifiable on the Registry side and 'baum-os: registered pin is not an ancestor of the observed head' on the Atlas side, all of which disappear after the mirror is refreshed. A CONTROLLED REPRODUCTION shows the class is larger than the observed instance: a baum-os mirror deliberately left behind the pull request 70 merge, fetched shallow with refs/remotes/origin/main at 2f4bd587, answers 547 verified current claims, 28 historical, 28 separate current observations, 82 diagnostics of which 74 are unverifiable, and 3 mismatches, against 617 verified, 8 diagnostics and 1 mismatch on the fresh farm - every baum-os commit newer than the mirror's head becomes unverifiable, and each false mismatch is indistinguishable in the output from a real drift. The gate verdict depends on the freshness of the local mirror, so the CI-faithful invocation is the one whose result can be relied on. THREE DEFECTS IN THIS LANE'S OWN RECORDS were found against the merged source and are repaired in this run: the Atlas claim named the PRE-REBASE commits (final published head 5541ccdf179e01236fe0c278dcc4b92423bcfcda, implementation commit 95c6ed43f88d9c00045900ff5ef0fc2bc695834e, main before merge 2f94f8c5eab6ae3216b9dd0551a03624a88fd55c) although the branch was rebased onto 808bfb09 before publication, so the published head is 1dbac8ce52d3c6ffac49ca005e239c6d61131c11 and the implementation commit is f9b1dbb3e041d87e7ff0b0d61596b33f9151e566, and the two named commits are not ancestors of origin/main; neither the Registry record nor the Atlas claim mentioned the hardlink guard C5 or the code CORPUS_PATH_MULTIPLE_LINKS, which the shipped code carries; and the Registry record contradicted itself about the base, its change_status_scope naming 2f94f8c5 while its structured field source_publication.main_commit_before_merge names 808bfb09. No CONTRACT_RECORD, PROVENANCE or SUPERSESSION class changes: core/contracts/behavioral-eval.schema.json is untouched, the behavioral-eval validator is untouched, the corpus content is untouched, the BehavioralEvalRecord format is untouched, nothing is superseded, and the evaluation output is digest-neutral. The primitive is a tool surface, not a registered contract. Per the consumer binding in AGENTS.md, NO_CHANGE requires no Registry write; the change registration for this run, the repair of this lane's own records and the attribution of the foreign drift are projected separately in the Unitera Registry, and the representation in the Unitera Atlas, after the source merge. No independent human approval is claimed.
